issues.description: README example diff is far broader than the PR's stated scope
issues.detail: The PR description says it updates test_examples, things_advanced.py, and the FAQ. The README.rst diff rewrites large parts of the tutorial example (formatting, StorageError.handle signature change, status code helper, bounded_stream switch, .format vs %). Mixing extensive cosmetic rewrites with a small behavior change makes review and bisection harder; consider splitting or trimming.

issues.description: StorageError.handle signature changed from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params)
issues.detail: In README.rst the static method signature was reordered. Falcon's add_error_handler historically expected (ex, req, resp, params) for older versions; the new (req, resp, ex, params) matches newer Falcon but silently changing documentation examples without a note can mislead users on older releases. Confirm this matches the supported Falcon version and call it out.

issues.description: FAQ example PostTest reads req.content_length bytes even when body is empty, conflating two cases
issues.detail: The example uses `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)`; with Content-Length=1 and empty body, the WSGI input may block or return b'' depending on the server, making the 400 branch behavior implementation-dependent rather than illustrative. Consider clarifying that simulate_post pads/truncates here, or use a simpler assertion to avoid teaching a fragile pattern.

issues.description: Unused pytest fixture parameters in new test cases
issues.detail: test_things_advanced takes (asgi, util, httpx, requests) but the new resp3/resp4 blocks only exercise the WSGI path via testing.simulate_post on advanced.app. If the existing test was meant to cover both ASGI and WSGI, the new POST assertions should likely be parametrized or duplicated for ASGI to match the PR checklist claim about both code paths.

issues.description: FAQ code snippet has minor style issues
issues.detail: `headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]` has a stray trailing comma inside a single-element list, and `assert(result.status == ...)` uses parentheses that make it look like a function call (a common pytest anti-pattern). Cleaning these up keeps the documented example idiomatic.

issues.description: bounded_stream switch in things_advanced not mentioned in newsfragment/docs
issues.detail: examples/things_advanced.py now uses req.bounded_stream.read() instead of req.stream.read(). This is a meaningful behavior change for the example (bounded_stream respects Content-Length) and is the crux enabling the new empty-body test, but there is no comment or newsfragment explaining why future readers should prefer bounded_stream here.

review.summary: The PR's stated intent (add POST tests + FAQ entry + tiny example fix) is reasonable, but the README.rst diff balloons the scope with formatting rewrites and a subtle StorageError.handle signature change that should not ride along silently. The new FAQ example teaches a slightly fragile pattern around content_length-bounded reads and has minor style issues. The new tests only exercise WSGI despite the test function accepting asgi/httpx fixtures, and the bounded_stream switch in things_advanced.py deserves a brief explanatory note.
